dehydrated = lacking enough water in the body
plant-based = made mainly or entirely from plants rather than animals
dairy-free = containing no milk or products made from milk
high-protein = containing a large amount of protein
low-carb = containing little starch or sugar
sugar-free = containing no added sugar
wholefood = food that is as close as possible to its natural state
eating disorder = a serious mental health condition involving harmful eating patterns
binge = an episode of eating a very large amount of food in a short time
comfort food = food you eat because it makes you feel emotionally better
emotional eating = eating in response to feelings rather than hunger
foodie = a person who is very interested in cooking and trying dishes
gourmet = connected with high-quality, carefully prepared food
nutritionist = a person who advises on food and nutrients, not always a regulated doctor
dietitian = a qualified health professional who gives evidence-based diet advice
fussy eater = a person who refuses many foods and accepts only a few
tip = extra money left for waiting staff for their service
reservation = an arrangement to have a table kept for you at a set time
Michelin star = a mark of excellence given to a restaurant by the Michelin guide
à la carte = ordered as individual dishes from a menu, not as a fixed set
